key_insight: A weakly supervised, MT-free approach can detect sentence-level editorial reuse across languages, identifying where and how news agencies copy or adapt sentences without requiring full translations — enabling fast pre-selection of reused content for journalists.
problem_solved: Detecting fine-grained, cross-lingual text reuse in news (sentence-level) despite limited parallel data and translation costs, reducing manual search and information overload for newsroom verification.
method: Weak supervision that leverages multilingual semantic signals (e.g., multilingual embeddings / alignment cues) and a small set of heuristics or seeds instead of large parallel corpora.
MT-free sentence-level similarity matching and thresholding to flag candidate reused sentences across languages, followed by ranking/prioritization for human review.
Integrates into an automated pre-selection workflow to present journalists with high-confidence reuse candidates and contextual article locations.
impact: Enables scalable, low-cost cross-lingual reuse detection useful for newsroom fact-checking and content provenance; for ML practitioners it demonstrates practical weak supervision strategies for multilingual retrieval and fine-grained similarity tasks in low-resource settings.
visual_elements: Pipeline flowchart: input articles → multilingual sentence encoder → similarity scoring → candidate ranking → journalist review

paper_title: Rewrite the News: Tracing Editorial Reuse Across News Agencies
paper_authors: Soveatin Kuntur, Nina Smirnova, Anna Wroblewska, Philipp Mayr, Sebastijan Razboršek Maček
